issue.title: Highlights quotes lose hard-wrapped lines that start with '# ' and render the rest of the quote as a Comment
issue.description:
## What is wrong

In linked-page Highlights sidecars, a highlight's hard-wrapped quote can contain a
physical line that starts with `# ` (a shell or code comment in the highlighted text),
written without a leading `>`. `is_quote_continuation_line`
(`src/native/highlights_ref/sidecar_render.rs`) rejects any `is_markdown_heading` line,
so the quote ends early at that line. `parse_sidecar_chunk`
(`src/native/highlights_ref/sidecar.rs`) then sends the rest of the quote to the comment
side and filters the heading-shaped line out entirely. Result: highlighted words are
silently dropped and the remainder of the quote is rendered as a `[!note] Comment`.

## Reproduction (real vault data, read-only)

1. `~/bob/lib/docs/gastown_readme.textbundle/text.markdown` lines 150-157: quote lines
   `> # Set custom agent command` ... `> --thinking low"` are followed by the bare line
   `# Set default agent`, then `gt config default-agent`, then `> claude-glm`.
   `~/bob/ref/docs/gastown_readme.md` lines 79-83 render the quote without
   "Set default agent" and show `Comment gt config default-agent > claude-glm`.
2. `~/bob/lib/chat/sase_listen_antennapod_setup.md` line 63: bare `# should start with <?xml`
   inside a quote. `~/bob/ref/chat/sase_listen_antennapod_setup.md` lines 51-55 drop that
   line and render `Comment > … <rss`.

A read-only awk scan of all 178 sidecars under `~/bob/lib` found exactly these two
cases of a `#`-led line directly after a `>` line. Real user comments are always
separated from their quote by a blank line (161 of 161 comments after a blank line;
0 list-style comments directly after a quote line).

## Likely fix

In linked style, treat a heading-shaped line that immediately follows a quote line
(no blank line between) as quote continuation text unless it is a page heading or an
annotation-date header. Keep the comment side starting only after a blank line.
Expect a one-time `^h-` re-mint (and tombstone) for the two affected highlights, since
their quote text changes; decide whether to accept that or add a reuse rule.

## Why it matters now

The planned section-annotation feature (`# <name>` declarations in Highlights notes)
must not read these quote lines as section declarations; the same boundary rule fixes
both.

task_type_fields.impact: Highlighted words vanish from two ref notes (gastown_readme p.8, sase_listen_antennapod_setup p.4) and quote text is shown as a user Comment in Obsidian, bob ref show, and the Mac Refs inspector.
task_type_fields.repro: Compare ~/bob/lib/docs/gastown_readme.textbundle/text.markdown lines 150-157 with ~/bob/ref/docs/gastown_readme.md lines 79-83, and ~/bob/lib/chat/sase_listen_antennapod_setup.md line 63 with ~/bob/ref/chat/sase_listen_antennapod_setup.md lines 51-55: the bare `# ...` quote line is missing from the rendered quote and the rest of the quote appears as a Comment callout.

issue.creation_reason: Found while researching section annotations: two real ref notes silently drop highlighted text and mislabel quote text as the user's comment, and the planned '# <name>' section grammar would misread the same lines.

payload.description: Both touch highlight ^h- identity; fixing the quote boundary changes the quote text and so re-mints the two affected IDs
Verify cld-filed quote/heading parser bug that gates section declarations
